meta.title: OxideTerm — Native SSH workspace for remote servers
meta.description: A free, native GPUI SSH client for remote servers: terminals, SFTP, port forwarding, remote editing, RDP/VNC, local shells, and BYOK OxideSens AI. No Electron, no telemetry, no subscription.

workbench.title: One connection, six surfaces
workbench.subtitle: Open a server once and keep terminals, transfers, tunnels, editing, and optional AI on the same node.
workbench.workspace_caption: GPU-rendered terminals alongside local shells and host tools.
workspace_points: Mix up to 16 panes of SSH, local shells, notes, SFTP, and remote desktops in one tab
Native tmux -CC control mode, split panes, broadcast input, and command folding
Triggers, regex search, session logs, and asciicast v2 recording and playback
workbench.demo_caption: Connect to a host, enter a Docker container, and edit a file in place.
demo_points: Start from a saved connection or imported ~/.ssh/config entry
Jump directly into a running container shell from the terminal
Open and save container files in the built-in editor without extra tools
workbench.demo_fallback: Your browser does not support video playback.
workbench.sftp_caption: Dual-pane local and remote files on the active SSH session.
sftp_points: Parallel transfer queue with speed limits, pause/resume, ETA, and SCP fallback
Built-in previews for code, Markdown, images, audio, video, hex, and fonts
Drop files onto a terminal to upload, or use trzsz and ZMODEM from the shell
workbench.ide_caption: Lightweight remote editing without launching a separate heavyweight IDE.
ide_points: Multi-tab editor with Git branch/staging status and project-wide regex search
Safe saves with conflict handling and preserved encoding and line endings
Works over SFTP or shell, with an optional Linux remote agent for fast indexing
workbench.forwarding_caption: Inspect listening ports and manage SSH tunnels visually.
forwarding_points: Local (-L), remote (-R), and dynamic SOCKS5 (-D) tunnels with one-click presets
Detects ports listening on the server and forwards them without typing flags
Automatically restores active forwards after a reconnect while keeping stopped rules off
workbench.ai_caption: Bring your own AI model, or expose your sessions via MCP.
ai_points: Works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, Ollama, or compatible endpoints
Redacts credentials before sending terminal or file context to any provider
Optional external MCP control lets Claude Code or Codex use your authenticated jump-host sessions

architecture.title: How it is built
architecture.subtitle: In-process Rust services, shared SSH transport, and explicit local trust boundaries.
architecture.multiplex_desc: NodeRouter shares one authenticated SSH connection across terminals, SFTP, port forwards, and the IDE. Multi-hop ProxyJump and TOTP prompts stay attached to the session.
architecture.runtime_desc: SSH bytes flow straight into Rust-owned terminal state and GPUI GPU draw calls inside one desktop process, with no WebView, JSON bridge, or xterm.js layer.
architecture.security_desc: Passwords and API keys stay in the OS keychain and are zeroized on drop. Exported .oxide bundles use ChaCha20-Poly1305 with Argon2id (256 MB, 4 iterations).
architecture.plugins_desc: Extend the app with declarative Manifest, sandboxed Wasmtime WASM, or Process plugins, reviewed for permissions before activation. Full UI support across 11 languages.

download.title: Install OxideTerm
download.subtitle: Available for macOS, Windows, and Linux
download.requirements: Licensed under GPL-3.0. No account or WebView runtime required.
download.macos_note: If you install from a DMG manually and Gatekeeper blocks it, run: xattr -cr /Applications/OxideTerm.app
download.windows_note: Scoop keeps CLI shims on PATH. If SmartScreen warns on manual .exe installs, choose More info → Run anyway.
download.linux_note: AppImage, .deb, and .rpm packages are published on GitHub. Set OXIDETERM_RENDER_PROFILE=compatibility if the window does not draw.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: Is OxideTerm free for commercial use?
faq.a1: Yes. OxideTerm is licensed under GPL-3.0-only with no paid tiers, seats, or telemetry. You can use it for personal, academic, or commercial work.
faq.q2: Which SSH authentication methods are supported?
faq.a2: Password, private keys (Ed25519, RSA, ECDSA), OpenSSH certificates, system SSH Agent, keyboard-interactive 2FA, built-in TOTP auto-fill, Kerberos, multi-hop ProxyJump, and FIDO security keys via plugin.
faq.q3: Does OxideTerm work offline without an account?
faq.a3: Yes. SSH, SFTP, port forwarding, local shells, and saved connections stay on your machine with credentials stored in your OS keychain. Cloud Sync and AI only connect when you configure a provider.
faq.q4: How do OxideSens AI and external MCP work?
faq.a4: OxideSens uses your own API key (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, Ollama, or compatible endpoints). You can also enable the built-in MCP server so external tools like Claude Code or Codex operate through your authenticated SSH connections.
faq.q5: Why russh instead of libssh2 or OpenSSL?
faq.a5: russh integrates directly with Rust and Tokio without requiring libssh2 or a system OpenSSL runtime. Secrets crossing credential boundaries are wrapped with zeroize.

legal.title: Compliance & Legal
legal.subtitle: OxideTerm is designed for legitimate system administration, development, and research.
legal.network_desc: OxideTerm is a remote server management and terminal tool intended solely for authorized system administration, network operations, development, and research. Users must comply with applicable laws when using SSH tunneling or port forwarding.
legal.ai_desc: OxideTerm stores AI conversation history locally. Requests and selected context go directly to the provider you configure under that provider's terms. OxideTerm operates no AI relay and collects no conversation data.
legal.data_desc: Core workflows need no OxideTerm account. Credentials stay in your OS keychain; Cloud Sync and AI connect only to providers you configure.
